page: Microsoft Azure L12aos_v4 is a storage-optimized server instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 12 virtual CPUs mapped to 6 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware configuration includes a substantial 8639 GB local NVMe SSD, making it highly capable for storage-intensive operations.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25% of tested hardware. Text processing and small-model LLM text generation also demonstrate strong performance. However, multi-core CPU execution, database operations, and web serving throughput fall within the average tier. A notable performance tradeoff is observed in memory bandwidth; while small-block cached reads are average, large-block uncached read memory bandwidth is weak, registering in the bottom 25% at 38.93 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L12aos_v4 offers a high density of local NVMe storage relative to its compute footprint, reducing the need for external premium storage attachments for large datasets. This resource profile is highly suitable for large-scale databases, data warehousing, indexing services, and memory-intensive applications that require rapid access to extensive local scratch space.
